answer: A hostile operator therefore has to keep each duplicate self continuously active for 20 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. The basalt counter is kept in mesa and sparrow shows each reset. A bond is refunded only after 20 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. That bill is paid per identity, so 88 aliases cost 188 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
